Ever since I was young, I have been fascinated by how machines work, and that curiosity grew into a clear commitment to building solutions that are efficient, reliable, and made to last. I am originally from Nigeria, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Across my academic and project work, I have completed 7 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex mechanical problems into designs that work not only in theory but also in production and use. One example came when I needed to use a new engineering tool for a project; within a few weeks I was using it confidently, and soon afterwards I was helping teammates set up their first models and avoid the early mistakes I had already worked through.

My experience has also shown me how much I value solving difficult technical problems in ways that can be applied beyond a single task. In one project, I developed an original solution to a mechanical design problem that others had not managed to resolve, and the approach was later taken up outside my own team for similar work. On another occasion, colleagues began coming to me with questions in my own area, asking me to review calculations or talk through design choices before they moved ahead. Beyond the technical side, one of my favourite memories was taking my family to a science and engineering exhibition where they saw a prototype I had helped develop and immediately started asking questions about every moving part. Hearing a younger relative proudly tell strangers, “They build things that actually work!” made this career feel especially meaningful. I am now eager to bring my training, practical mindset, and enthusiasm to a Mechanical Engineer role where I can contribute dependable solutions and continue growing through real engineering challenges.

reference_text:
Few roles bring together stories, learning, and public service as naturally as librarianship, which is why I have built my career around helping people find exactly the right information. What continues to engage me is the way a library can turn curiosity into confidence, whether someone is beginning a research project, looking for their next novel, or simply searching for a welcoming place to start. My perspective was shaped further through doctoral study at a university ranked in the global top 100, where I completed a Doctorate and saw how access to well-organised knowledge can change the pace and quality of people’s work. That experience taught me to approach questions by looking not only at the information requested, but also at the clearest route to it. Pursuing a Librarian role is therefore a natural continuation of what has long motivated me: a love of stories, learning, and helping people discover resources that feel both useful and inviting.

This led me to seek out practical ways to improve access and support others. In one role, I needed to use a new digital tool for organising and retrieving materials; within a few weeks I was using it confidently, and soon afterwards I was showing colleagues how to get started so they could use it in their own work. When a recurring issue in locating and tracking frequently requested items was slowing the team down, I introduced a simple workaround that streamlined the process and reduced repeated delays. Colleagues also sometimes came to me with questions in my own area, and I became someone they would ask when they wanted help untangling a search or identifying the most relevant source. Across my work, I have completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, and I bring that same practical focus to every setting. Originally from Colombia, I am especially drawn to creating welcoming spaces where curiosity can grow for people of all ages. One of my favourite memories is watching a young family member proudly use their very first library card at one of my community events, then asking me to recommend “a book with adventure and dragons.” That moment captured exactly why this work matters to me, and what I hope to contribute as a librarian.

Everyday events rarely feel ordinary to me; I have always been drawn to the stories beneath them, and journalism quickly became the clearest way to turn that curiosity into public service through clear, responsible reporting. That motivation deepened through moments that showed me how closely reporting can sit within people’s lives. One of my favourite memories is bringing a family member to a local community event I was covering, only for them to recognise someone I was interviewing from a story they had followed for years. Seeing that connection unfold in real time confirmed why I want to build my career in journalism: to investigate carefully, listen closely, and give space to perspectives that might otherwise be missed. I am from France and hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100, where I developed the discipline to work through complex material and carry ideas through to completion, including 7 completed projects with tangible outcomes.

That academic foundation has been matched by practical habits that shape how I work. When I needed to use a new digital research and publishing tool for a fast-moving project, I set aside focused time over several months to learn it well enough to contribute independently and meet deadlines without hand-holding. In one team setting, a recurring workflow problem was repeatedly delaying progress, so I mapped where the hold-up occurred and introduced a simpler workaround that the group could use immediately, reducing the disruption to day-to-day work. Colleagues and supervisors have also regularly come to me with difficult questions, including ones outside my own area, such as when I was asked to help untangle a complicated issue and turn it into a clear explanation others could use.

What I most want to bring to my next role is the ability to translate complex, fast-moving information into accurate, compelling stories that readers can quickly understand and trust. Looking ahead, I am eager to continue developing as a journalist who reports with speed, depth, and care, while making a meaningful contribution through curiosity, consistency, and continuous learning.
